choices.reasoning: Strong opening: Maria Hill (draws a card), Hawkeye, Triskelion, and Genius to fund them. Keep all six.
Clock check: T 0/6 (+~3 hero, +~8 alter-ego — cannot end in alter-ego), HP 12 vs ~3 incoming. Build board first: use Commander to draw before playing anything, as alter-ego ability.
Play Maria Hill first (her response draws a card); pay exactly with Genius (2 mental).
Exact payment with Genius preserves Energy Absorption (3 energy) to fund Hawkeye's full cost.
Free extra card — always take it.
Play Hawkeye now, funded by Energy Absorption (exact 3 energy), building the board before acting.
Exact single-card payment; keeps my events (Photonic Blast, Get Ready) in hand.
Play Triskelion to unlock the 4-ally limit; will pay with Make the Call, which currently has no ally target in discard.
Make the Call has no ally in my discard to target, while Get Ready and Photonic Blast both have live uses next turn.
Clear the crisis side scheme: Maria removes 2 of its 3 threat (crisis otherwise blocks main-scheme thwarting).
Hawkeye's 1 THW finishes the last threat on Defense Network exactly, removing the crisis icon.
Crisis cleared; must end the turn in hero form — ending in alter-ego would add ~8 threat vs the 6 threshold.
Weapons Runner is only ATK/SCH 1 — not dangerous per target priority; push damage on Klaw's 12-HP stage.

Hawkeye has 2 HP: he can attack now (→1 HP), readies at end of phase anyway, and still defends or acts next turn. Maria at 1 HP would die to the consequential damage — she's my THW-2 answer for next turn's main scheme.
Push Klaw to 9 HP; Weapons Runner (1/1) is not a priority target.
Only one card in hand (Photonic Blast, my 5-damage event) — keep it and draw 4.

12 HP vs Klaw's ATK 0 + ~2 boost + Weapons Runner's 1 ≈ 3 damage — no danger. Both 1-HP allies are more valuable ready to act (Maria THW-2, Hawkeye attack) next turn than dying or going exhausted here; no damage-prevention card in hand (Emergency only counters scheming).
Only 1 damage vs 10 HP; defending with Captain Marvel would cost my basic attack next turn, and either 1-HP ally would die for it.
Draw/resources first: Rechannel heals 1 (9→10) and draws a card, fueling it with Emergency — my least useful card since I'm staying in hero form and Emergency only counters scheming.
Emergency is 1 energy and the least valuable card (only counters scheming); save Energy (2) for paying costs.
Nick Fury is the swing play: 4 damage / 3 draws / 2 threat plus ATK 2 (kills Weapons Runner exactly), and his 3 HP Temporary body is the perfect defender for round 2's villain phase.

Keep Avengers Mansion — its draw engine outvalues Photonic Blast's one-time 5 damage over the remaining ~8 rounds. Fury's ATK kills Weapons Runner, his body defends round 2, and I'll take the 4-damage choice.

My hand is nearly empty (Mansion only). Draw 3 refills options — likely enabling Mansion or an ally this round — while Klaw's stage 1 (9 HP) dies next turn regardless, which also delays the Immortal Klaw's acceleration by a round.
Fury's ATK 2 kills Weapons Runner exactly (permanent -1 damage/round), before he leaves play — chip damage on Klaw can wait since I lack the burst to cross stages cleanly anyway.
Only 1 threat exists — a thwart wastes over half its value, and the scheme advances round 3 with or without it. Guaranteed 2 damage on Klaw instead.

Spider-Woman brings a 2/2 body that acts this turn plus her confuse — which makes future alter-ego (Commander) turns nearly threat-free. Fury is Temporary and leaves at round end anyway, so he's the ally I'll shed for the slot.
Fury is Temporary (leaves at round end regardless) and has already used his attack to kill Weapons Runner; Maria and Hawkeye both have a final act left next turn.
Free confuse: Klaw's next scheme does nothing, which makes a future alter-ego (Commander draw) turn nearly threat-free.
Spider-Woman's 2 damage pushes Klaw to 5; Maria and Hawkeye keep their final acts for next turn where they can also choose between damage, threat, or defending.

Clocks: T 1/6 (advances round 3 regardless, not a loss), HP 10 vs ~2 incoming (Klaw ATK 0 + boosts, no minions) — both safe. Maria and Hawkeye's final acts are worth more next turn (damage, threat or defense of choice); hand is empty so I draw 5.
No attack-cancel card in hand; Klaw's boost is typically ~2 vs my 10 HP — safe to take. All three 1-HP allies keep their final acts for next turn's stage-1 kill.
Whirlwind is ATK 2 (dangerous per priority rules) with 6 HP — starting him at 4 with Hawkeye's free arrow counter response makes him killable next turn while I still kill Klaw's stage.
Draw first: Rechannel heals to 11 and draws a card, paid with the wild Power of Leadership (only listed energy source — my other cards are physical).
Lead from the Front buffs hero + all 3 allies (+1 ATK/THW each) — that's 10 damage this turn, enough to kill Whirlwind (4) and Klaw's stage 1 (5) outright.
Strength alone covers the cost exactly, keeping Helicarrier, Helmet and Get Ready — next turn's 6-card hand can establish Helicarrier and Helmet both.
Buffed Maria's 2 damage + Hawkeye's 2 will kill Whirlwind (4) exactly — dangerous ATK-2 minion down with zero overkill; stage 1's 2 remaining HP I finish with basic next turn exactly.
Hawkeye's buffed 2 finishes Whirlwind exactly.

Buffed basic puts stage 1 at exactly 2 — my unbuffed basic of 2 kills it with zero overkill next turn, while the alternative (with Spider-Woman) overkills 1 and starts the Immortal Klaw acceleration a round earlier.
End-turn check: T2 + ~3 alter-ego threat < 6; Klaw is confused so his scheme does nothing (the ideal moment for alter-ego); gains hand-size 6, Commander draw, and dodges all attack damage this phase.
Free card before ending the turn — alter-ego ability is why I changed form.

Nothing here beats holding: round 4 starts in alter-ego with hand size 6 (drawing 2) plus Commander, and I can then pick Helicarrier, Helmet, or Photonic Blast based on that draw — playing Helmet now would burn cards I may need, and Spider-Woman's act can wait.
Below hand size — no discard, draw 2.
Alter-ego ability before form change — free card, and I need every resource for this turn's plays (Inspired, Photonic Blast, maybe Helicarrier).
Free healing before form change (11→12); the alter-ego turn's whole point was recovery and card advantage.
Free upgrade (0 cost) — a future energy dump that turns spare energy cards into 2 damage each.

Inspired buffs Spider-Woman to 3/3 for both her remaining attacks; Energy Channel stays uncharged for now since Energy Absorption must pay Photonic Blast — Melter dies this turn or I face 3 ATK plus forced defends every round.
Helmet is the lowest-value card here (only matters when I personally defend); Get Ready doubles a fresh ally next turn and Photonic+Energy Absorption must stay paired for the Melter kill.

Revised plan: pay Helicarrier with Energy Absorption — then Spider-Woman (3, buffed) + basic (2) kills Melter exactly anyway, Helicarrier's discount goes live for next turn, and Photonic Blast stays in hand as a held 5-damage answer.
Must end in hero form anyway (T3 + alter-ego threat ≥ 6), and no more alter-ego actions remain.
Buffed Spider-Woman's 3 + my basic 2 = Melter's 5 exactly — the ATK-3 forced-defend minion dies this turn with zero waste.

Recovering as Carol left her exhausted and form-change preserves exhaustion — my basic attack is gone for this turn (a mistake I'm absorbing). Nothing else is playable or targeted; Melter's last 2 HP survive to the villain phase and I take the hits.
Below hand size — keep both (Photonic is my held 5-damage answer, Get Ready doubles an ally next turn) and draw 3.
Klaw's ATK 0 + boosts ≈ 2 vs my 12 HP — no defender (per rule step 4: a hero that defend loses next turn's basic attack, worth more than DEF 1 saves). I need the hero ready for round 5.
HP is critical at 3 after that brutal phase (Klaw 3, Melter 3+3) — First Aid heals 2, paid with the dead Get Ready (no allies to target).
Get Ready has no ally to target — it's a 1-resource dead card; save Photonic, Haymaker and Lead for damage.

Heal to 6 and draw before attacking; sacrifice Lead from the Front as the energy — it's my worst card (needs allies I don't have), while Haymaker and Photonic both stay as self-sufficient damage next turn.
Lead from the Front needs allies and a 2-cost payment to matter; Haymaker works standalone as 3 damage.

Clock check: T4 + hero threat (~1 round + ~2 encounter) = 7 ≥ 6 — scheme in danger, so removing threat comes first. Crisis Interdiction takes T to 2 (2+3 = 5 < 6, advance averted); it burns Photonic and Haymaker as payment, but stage 2's raw stats would make a kill-both turn too dangerous at 6 HP.

My basic attack is gone (hero was exhausted by round-4 boosts) and my hand is empty — ending in hero form at HP 6 means facing Klaw + Melter attacks plus an encounter card, likely death. Changing to Carol converts both activations to scheming (no damage at all) and unlocks round-6 REC 4 healing and hand size 6. Yes, T2 + ~6-8 alter-ego threat overshoots 6 and advances the main scheme — a setback — but survival beats an advanced scheme.
Free card before ending the turn.
Nothing left to play — hand size 6 in alter-ego means I draw 5 fresh cards.
Below hand size — Make the Call is great right now (Maria Hill and Spider-Woman sit in my discard to re-recruit). Draw 5.

The main scheme advanced to the final stage (threshold 8) — no more alter-ego shelter, so round 6 I must end as hero facing ~6-10 damage at 6 HP. Only REC 4 healing (which requires Carol ready) keeps me alive; the stun just taxes my basic attack (allies and events still deal damage) and one surge card is cheaper than near-certain death.
Commander first — draw before spending resources.
REC 4 first — this is the survival turn: 6→10 HP before ending in hero form against Klaw, Armored Guard and Radioactive Man.
Recruit Maria Hill (THW 2 body that draws on entry) — funding the plan: this payment burns Crisis + Alpha Flight Station, keeping Inspired and Vision to pay discounted Mockingbird next.
Burn Crisis + Alpha Flight Station (lowest future value with threat at 1/8) to recruit Maria — keeps Inspired, Vision and Energy Channel to fund discounted Mockingbird next.
Free card.

Mockingbird in — her entry stun goes to Melter (ATK 3 + forced ally-defend ≈ 4 damage saved next phase); payment will burn Inspired and the duplicate Energy Channel, keeping Vision and Photonic Blast.
Cancel — I forgot to arm the Helicarrier discount first, which would make Mockingbird cost 2 instead of 3 and save a card.
Arm the discount before playing Mockingbird (3→2).
Discounted Mockingbird (2) paid with Inspired + the duplicate Energy Channel — keeps Vision and Photonic Blast as next turn's firepower, and her stun hits Melter.
Keeps Vision and Photonic Blast — the damage pair for next turn.
Stun Melter — his ATK 3 plus forced ally-defend is the biggest incoming threat; the stun nullifies his whole next attack.
Melter's ATK 3 + forced defend is ~4 damage — the other enemies cap around 1-2 each.
Mockingbird pops Armored Guard's tough status first (any hit absorbs it entirely).
Maria's 1 drops the Guard to 2 HP — next turn Mockingbird + Vision finish it and the villain becomes attackable.
Must end in hero: alter-ego threat next phase would be ~7-8 (Klaw's 4-scheme + minions) putting T1+8 at the loss threshold exactly. HP 10 can take the attacks.
Below hand size — Vision and Photonic Blast both earn their slots next turn. Draw 3.

Hero DEF 1 absorbs the boost damage; the cost is normally losing next turn's basic attack, but my basic is stun-wasted this round or next anyway, so I defend cheaply and keep both allies' final acts for clearing the Guard.

Just 1 damage (7→6). Mockingbird defending would keep her exhausted through all of round 7 (defenders ready only at end of next player phase) and Maria would die — I need both ready next turn: Maria+Mockingbird kill the 2-HP Guard exactly and Vision kills Klaw's 2-HP stage exactly.

Maria defends: her 1 HP absorbs the hit and (since the ally is the one attacked) I also dodge the random hand discard. Losing her is cheaper than HP 5 plus a 40% chance my rip hits Vision or Photonic Blast — next turn Mockingbird+Vision still clear Guard and Klaw exactly.
Arm Helicarrier discount — Photonic Blast will cost 2 instead of 3, freeing exactly one energy card for a 1-counter Energy Channel charge.
Mockingbird pops the tough on the 3-HP Armored Guard (#47) first so Photonic Blast's 5 damage lands fully.
Tough is gone — Photonic's 5 kills the 3-HP Guard outright (overkill is unavoidable here, but both guards must fall to unblock the villain).
Both Crisis cards pay — leaves Tenacity's energy to charge Energy Channel for the exact kill on the other Guard.

Catastrophe: Photonic Blast was blocked by my own stun (Hero Action (attack) — I forgot it was never popped), so both Crisis cards bought nothing. With only Tenacity left, the best use is charge → fire 2 damage for the exact kill on Armored Guard #48 — killing Melter instead computes to certain death (the remaining four attackers outdamage HP 4 regardless), while #48's death removes one full attack.
Exact kill on the 2-HP Guard — removes one incoming attack permanently.
Guard #48 dies exactly; Melter's attack gets absorbed by forced-defending Mockingbird anyway, so the Guard's guaranteed 1 damage is the one I must delete.
Hand is empty and I must stay in hero form (alter-ego threat next phase would hit the 8 threshold). End turn: draw 5, then Mockingbird forced-defends Melter while my hero defends Klaw.
Hero defends Klaw (DEF 1 shaves the boosts) — Mockingbird must stay ready for Melter's forced ally-defend, since if she can't answer that trigger he hits me for his full 3 undefended.

choices.reasoning: Make the Call has no target until an ally is in my discard pile, so it is dead for the first several rounds; swapping it for a fresh card is low-risk while keeping Mockingbird (stun for Tiger Shark), Inspired, Crisis Interdiction (must clear the crisis side scheme), Avengers Mansion (long game vs 12/18/22 HP stages), and Lead from the Front.

Keep: Mockingbird (ally + stun for Tiger Shark), Inspired (cheap ally buff), Crisis Interdiction (needed to clear the crisis side scheme), Avengers Mansion (long-game engine vs Klaw's 12/18/22 HP stages), and Lead from the Front (energy buff event). Round 1 plan: Commander draw, play Mockingbird and stun Tiger Shark, change to hero (must not end in alter-ego — alter-ego threat would hit the 6-threat threshold), thwart Defense Network.

Clock check: T 0/6 (+1/round hero, ~+8 alter-ego vs threshold 6 — cannot end in alter-ego), HP 12 vs ~5 incoming (Tiger Shark ATK 3 + Klaw 0 ATK + 2 boosts), 52 total villain HP means a long game. Draw first in alter-ego per procedure before playing anything.

Play Mockingbird to stun Tiger Shark (prevents his ATK 3 attacks and post-attack tough). Payment will use the three least-valuable cards, keeping Inspired (round-2 TS kill), Crisis Interdiction (clear the crisis side scheme), and Avengers Mansion (long-game engine).

Pay Mockingbird with Lead from the Front, Emergency, and Photonic Blast — the three cards I value least for the next two turns. This keeps Inspired (buffs Mockingbird for a round-2 Tiger Shark kill), Crisis Interdiction (must clear Defense Network), and Avengers Mansion (long-game draw engine).

choices.reasoning: Stun Tiger Shark: his ATK 3 attacks are the main incoming damage, and stunning him prevents the attack plus his post-attack tough status. Klaw only has ATK 0 + boosts.
Tiger Shark's ATK 3 attacks each round are the bigger threat; stunning him prevents the damage and his post-attack tough status. Klaw's ATK is only 0 + boosts.
Must end the turn as hero (alter-ego threat would reach ~8 vs threshold 6). Change form now so I can use my basic attack; Mockingbird will thwart Defense Network either form.

Clock check: T 0/6 (+1/round, safe), HP 12 vs ~2-5 incoming (Tiger Shark stunned round 1), win clock long (52 total villain HP). Tiger Shark at 6 HP: this 2 damage plus Mockingbird's thwart now, then next turn hero 2 + Mockingbird 2 (with Inspired) = 4 kills him exactly before he can attack. Defense Network sits at 3 with no growth — clearing it costs both basic powers this turn and would leave Tiger Shark alive to attack for 3 next villain phase.

Mockingbird thwarts Defense Network (3→2). Keeping Inspired and Avengers Mansion in hand: next turn Inspired on Mockingbird plus hero attack = 4 damage kills Tiger Shark exactly, and Crisis Interdiction can then clear the side scheme.

All basic powers are exhausted and Inspired cannot be paid for without discarding Mansion or Crisis, both of which I need next turn. Ending in hero form: T 0 + ~1-3 next-phase threat is safely under 6, Tiger Shark is stunned so only Klaw attacks (~0 ATK + 2 boosts), and HP 12 is healthy. Keeping Inspired, Crisis Interdiction, and Avengers Mansion for round 2.
Hand has only 3 cards vs hand size 5, so no discards — draw up to 5. Keeping Inspired, Crisis Interdiction, and Avengers Mansion.

Round-2 plan needs both Captain Marvel's basic attack (2) and Mockingbird's attack (2, buffed by Inspired) to kill Tiger Shark exactly (4 HP) before he attacks — defending with either would leave them exhausted next turn and Tiger Shark would attack for 3 plus gain tough. Klaw's base ATK is 0 plus 2 boosts (planning ~2); HP 12 absorbs it. No damage-prevention cards in hand.

Clock check: T 1/6 (+~3 next phase, safe), HP 7 vs ~5 incoming if Tiger Shark dies (dangerous if he lives — must kill him this turn). Play Photonic Blast at Klaw (5 damage, stage 1 of 3 with 52 total HP — every point counts) paid with Energy Absorption (3 energy) which also triggers the +1 card draw; that drawn card funds Inspired on Mockingbird, whose 2 ATK plus my basic 2 kills Tiger Shark exactly (4 HP), leaving both my basic powers free and keeping Avengers Mansion in hand.

Energy Absorption alone covers the 3 cost and is paid with an energy resource, triggering Photonic Blast's draw-1. This keeps Inspired (needed to buff Mockingbird for the Tiger Shark kill), Crisis Interdiction (side scheme), and Avengers Mansion (engine).

HP 7 with ~4-5 incoming next villain phase makes healing a priority; Rechannel (heal 1 → 8, draw 1) is free with Crisis Interdiction as the only energy card, and Crisis is redundant — Mockingbird (THW 2 with Inspired) clears Defense Network next turn while my basic THW 2 covers the main scheme. The drawn card replaces Crisis as Mansion fuel.

Must kill Tiger Shark this turn: hero 2 + buffed Mockingbird 2 = exactly his 4 HP, before he attacks for 3 plus gains tough (HP 8 can't absorb Klaw boosts + encounter + Tiger Shark ~8 damage). Pay Inspired with the duplicate copy; Avengers Mansion plus the new Energy card stay in hand to fund Mansion (4) next turn.
Pay with the duplicate Inspired — least valuable card since only one can attach per ally. Keeps Avengers Mansion (engine) and Energy (2 resources, half of Mansion's cost next turn).
Clock check: HP 8 vs ~7-8 incoming next phase if Tiger Shark lives (Klaw boosts + encounter + his ATK 3) — he must die now. Hero attack deals 2 of the exact 4 needed.
Mockingbird's buffed 2 ATK finishes Tiger Shark (2 HP) before his villain-phase attack — prevents 3 damage and his post-attack tough status.

Clock check: T 1/6, hero threat next phase ~3 → safe; HP 8 vs ~5 incoming (Tiger Shark dead, Klaw ATK 0 + 2 boosts + encounter card) → survivable; nothing left ready or payable (Mansion needs 4, only Energy with 2 in hand). Ending in hero form — alter-ego threat would be ~7, putting T + threat at 8 ≥ 6.
Only 2 cards vs hand size 5 — keep Avengers Mansion and Energy (they fund Mansion's 4 cost next turn) and draw 3.

Defending with the hero would exhaust her for round 3 (delaying the side-scheme clear and stage kill a full round); Mockingbird has only 1 HP and would die to any boost. Taking ~2-3 damage from Klaw's 0 ATK + 2 boosts is affordable at HP 8.

HP 1 is critical — Rechannel heals to 2 and draws a card, digging for an ally to chump-block next villain phase or more healing. Paying with the least useful energy card (Lead from the Front), keeping Energy for Avengers Mansion's 4 cost.

Lead from the Front is the worst of the energy cards here (a damage buff when my priority is healing/survival, not attacking), and keeping Energy (2) + Triskelion (1) + Power of Leadership (1) exactly funds Avengers Mansion's 4 cost next.

Clock check: T 3 + hero threat 3 = 6 ≥ 6 → scheme in danger (will clear Defense Network with my basic and Mockingbird's on the main scheme); HP 2 vs incoming ~3-5 → critical, and I have no blocker in hand, so Avengers Mansion's draw is my best dig for an ally to chump-block or prevention/healing. Paying with Energy + Strength keeps The Triskelion and The Power of Leadership (2 resources, plus Triskelion is playable).
Pay with Energy + Strength (exactly 4). This keeps The Triskelion (playable for 1 or fuel) and The Power of Leadership (1-2 wild resources) as the most flexible leftover hand.

Draw first before deciding anything else — I'm at HP 2 with no blocker, so I need to see whether Mansion's draw finds an ally, healing, or prevention. Keeping The Triskelion and The Power of Leadership as fuel for now (the +1 ally slot isn't needed with only Mockingbird in play).

choices.reasoning: Avengers Mansion costs 4 — too expensive for round 1 alongside my intended plays (Mockingbird + Arc Reactor). Under my plan it would only be fuel anyway, so I mulligan it for a chance at a cheaper card or one with 2 resources.
Hand has my planned round-1 plays (Mockingbird to stun Tiger Shark, Arc Reactor for Tech/ready), plus Helicarrier economy, Emergency and Repulsor Blast as flexible fuel.
Clock check: T 0/6, alter-ego next phase ~4-5 threat vs 6 target, hero ~3; HP 9 vs ~2-5 incoming. First action per procedure: use the draw/resource ability (Futurist) before playing anything.

Genius is worth 2 resources — it stretches my 7-card budget so I can play Mockingbird + Arc Reactor and still keep Repulsor Blast for next turn. Uppercut/Supersonic Punch are attack events I can't afford to fire this round anyway (they'd just be 1-resource fuel).
Mockingbird stuns Tiger Shark on entry — removes his 3-ATK attack and tough-gain — and gives me a 1/1 ally. Playing her before form change since she's form-agnostic.
Pay exactly 3 with Emergency + Genius, preserving Repulsor Blast (playable next turn for 1) and Arc Reactor (my planned second play, paid with the remaining two 1-resource cards).
Stun Tiger Shark: his 3 ATK hits harder than Klaw's, and stunning him stops his tough-status gain too.
Tiger Shark attacks for 3 each round and gains tough after attacking; stunning him removes the biggest single damage source. Klaw only attacks for ~0 + boosts.
Arc Reactor (Tech) raises my hero hand size and readies Iron Man — far more valuable for Iron Man than Helicarrier, which would cost me both Arc Reactor and Repulsor to pay for.
Keeps Repulsor Blast: with hero hand size 2 next turn, its cost of 1 is payable with the one other card in hand, while Haymaker/Helicarrier would be stuck unaffordable.
Board built (Mockingbird + Arc Reactor). Flipping to hero now to use basic powers, Arc Reactor's ready, and clear the crisis side scheme.
Start clearing Defense Network (crisis) — Mockingbird thwarts 1 (3→2). Will finish with Iron Man's THW 2, then use Arc Reactor to ready for an attack.
Iron Man's THW 2 finishes Defense Network (2→0), removing the crisis lock on main-scheme thwarting.
Arc Reactor readies Iron Man so I get my basic attack this turn instead of losing it to the thwart.
Push the villain clock — Tiger Shark has no guard, and Klaw's HP is the win condition. Damage to Tiger Shark can wait while he's stunned.
Repulsor Blast is exactly what I want for round 2: cost 1, payable with the single card I'm about to draw, for solid hero damage.

Klaw's base ATK is 0 + 2 boosts (expected ~0-4, usually ~1-2) vs my full 9 HP. Defending would exhaust Iron Man into my turn and cost Arc Reactor's ready; Mockingbird (2 HP) could die to a high roll. Not worth it — take the damage and stay ready to attack.

Clocks: T 1/6 (+~3 hero, no advance this round), HP 8 vs incoming ~4 (Klaw ~1 + Tiger Shark 3 + Melter 3, one body blocks). Win needs ~8 rounds but HP only lasts ~2 — so the turn serves the HP clock: focus Melter (5 HP) with all ~6 damage (Repulsor + Iron Man ×2 via Arc Reactor + Mockingbird); kill probability ~80%+. Keeping Mockingbird alive to block Tiger Shark next round.

I mis-targeted Repulsor at Klaw (option 1 was Klaw, not a generic play) — damage went to Klaw instead of Melter. Adapting: only 3 damage left (Iron Man ×2 + Mockingbird), not enough to kill Melter (5) this turn, so I'll put all 3 into Melter as prep: at 2 HP he dies to Iron Man's basics alone next turn, freeing my drawn cards for Tiger Shark. Mockingbird dies to Melter's forced-defense next round either way, so her consequential damage doesn't matter.
Readies Iron Man for his second attack on Melter.
Continue focusing Melter down to 2 HP.
Melter to 2 HP — then he dies to Iron Man's two basics alone next turn (1+1=2), no card resources needed.
Staying hero: T will be ~4 after this villain phase, and alter-ego threat (~7+) would exceed the 6 threshold — ending in alter-ego is never legal here. Nothing left to use.

Scenario analysis: Mockingbird must stay ready to absorb Melter's forced-ally-defense (she dies either way, blocking 3). The choice is whether Iron Man also defends (saving ~1 HP but exhausting him into round 3) or takes everything. Iron Man defending breaks my guaranteed round-3 plan: Melter at 2 dies to Iron Man's two basics (1+Arc Reactor+1) with NO cards needed, leaving both drawn cards for Tiger Shark. Without that guaranteed kill, Melter (3 ATK/round) lives on and the survival odds drop (est. ~40% survival keeping Iron Man ready vs ~20% defending). Klaw's 0+boosts can't defeat me from 8 HP.

Checked my drawn hand (Rocket Boots + Chase Them Down): neither deals damage. If Iron Man defends Tiger (HP 5→3), he's exhausted into round 3, Arc Reactor gives him only ONE attack, and Melter survives at 1 HP — then round-3 face damage is ≥5 vs my 3 = guaranteed loss. Taking the 3 (HP 5→2) keeps Iron Man ready: his two basics with Arc Reactor exactly kill Melter (2 HP) next turn. Then Rocket Boots (played, paying Chase Them Down) gives hand size 3 → three fresh cards at end of turn as my only remaining out (damage-prevention window, or the stage advancing to unlock an alter-ego heal). Mockingbird must stay ready to absorb Melter's forced defense regardless.

Play Rocket Boots (Tech) to raise hand size to 3 — three fresh cards at end of turn are my only real hope of drawing an attack-prevention interrupt for the deadly villain phase ahead (Klaw now 1+boosts with a stun attachment, Tiger Shark 3, my HP is 2). Chase Them Down as payment: threat is not my death clock.
Melter (2 HP) must die this turn — both basics go to him exactly.
Ready Iron Man for the killing blow on Melter.
Finish Melter — removes his 3 ATK from the villain phase.
Melter dead. Ending as hero — ending in alter-ego is illegal (T ~2 + alter-ego threat ~8 ≥ threshold 6). Drawing 3 now via the increased hand size.

HP 3 vs minimum incoming 3 (Klaw 1+boosts, Tiger 3) — every line is exactly at the edge of lethal. Defending Klaw minimizes his contribution (b after DEF 1) and may avoid the Sonic Converter stun at b=0. I also hold First Aid (heal 2) hoping the engine opens a response window before Tiger Shark's attack, which would lift HP to 5 and make survival possible.

choices.reasoning: Strong opening: three Tech upgrades (Arc Reactor + 2x Powered Gauntlets) that raise Iron Man's tiny hero hand size, plus Tac Team and Repulsor Blast for damage and Strength as flexible resources. Nothing worth discarding.
Clocks: T 0/7 (stage 1), HP 9; first action should be card draw/resources before playing. Futurist is free, once per round, and digs a card — use it before spending anything.

Genius (2 mental) is the only pick whose 2 resources complete payment for all three Tech upgrades this turn; Tech upgrades permanently raise Iron Man's tiny hero hand size, and resource cards are the designated fuel per the payment rule.

Board first: Arc Reactor is a Tech upgrade (raises hero hand size) and its ready effect is Iron Man's core damage engine. Paying with Strength alone leaves Repulsor Blast + Tac Team as exact fuel for the second Tech upgrade, keeping the second Gauntlet and Combat Training in hand for next turn.
Strength's double physical pays Arc Reactor alone, preserving Tac Team + Repulsor Blast as the exact 1+1 payment for the second Tech upgrade next.
Second Tech upgrade: hand-size +1 permanently. Paying with Tac Team + Repulsor Blast (1+1) keeps the other Gauntlet and Combat Training in hand so all three Techs are in play by next turn.
Exact 1+1 payment that spends the event and support I had earmarked as fuel, keeping both remaining cards (second Gauntlet, Combat Training) to finish the Tech package next turn.

Clocks: T 0/7, +~4 alter-ego threat next phase (still under 7); HP 9 vs 0 incoming as alter-ego. Ending in alter-ego refills to 6 (keeping Gauntlet + Combat Training plus 4 fresh), so both remaining Tech upgrades hit the table next turn and I flip to hero with a full build — flipping now would leave hand size 3 and stall the Tech package while eating a free attack.
Hand is only 2 cards vs size 6 — keep both Tech cards and draw 4.
Free interrupt (cost 0) that cuts this scheme by 1 threat; it only works while Rhino schemes (my alter-ego phases), so this is the moment to spend it. Against a 7-threat limit every point matters.
Use the card-draw action before spending anything, per the turn procedure — the pick may add exactly the fuel or a better play to this turn's plan.

Third Tech upgrade goes down; paying with the double-resource Energy leaves Combat Training + Repulsor Blast + Avengers Mansion (exactly 3 icons) as the exact payment for Mark V Armor.
Energy's two resources exactly cover the Gauntlet, keeping the other three cards whose icons sum to exactly Mark V Armor's cost of 3.

Last free damage action this turn.

HP 15 vs incoming ~4 (2 + high boost) — no danger, no prevention card in hand, and no allies. Defending would exhaust Iron Man through my next turn and cost a basic power; taking the hit preserves the full attack/thwart cycle.

Second gauntlet hit to finish Whiplash at 1 HP.

Ready for the second basic thwart on Breakin' & Takin'.

Pay Mockingbird with the three least valuable cards — the redundant second Rocket Boots (hand size already at the cap), Stark Tower (alter-ego-only action while I'm riding out the game in hero form), and Tigra — deliberately leaving Uppercut's physical icon to pay Relentless Assault so it gains overkill against the Guard minion.
